title: Former RAAF pilot convicted of murder after staging wife’s death as lawnmower accident
summary:
Brisbane supreme court jury finds Robert John Crawford guilty of murder after he stood to lose financially in divorce settlement

  • Get our

blocks.text: Former air force pilot Robert John Crawford has been found guilty of the murder of his wife after a jury accepted her death was staged as a fatal lawnmower accident.
Gasps and sobs could be heard in Brisbane supreme court on Friday after the jury returned a guilty verdict after deliberating since 10am on Tuesday.
Robert Crawford did not visually react to the verdict.
Frances Crawford’s body was found by paramedics at the bottom of a retaining wall near an overturned ride-on lawnmower at 4am.
Her husband was attempting to resuscitate her.
Robert Crawford was accused of murdering Frances Crawford by strangulation at the couple’s property, west of Brisbane, in the early hours of 30 July 2024, or late on 29 July.
Over three-and-a-half weeks, jurors heard evidence that included police forensic analysis of Frances Crawford’s injuries, texts between the couple and a UK forensic physician called by the defence.
They also visited the Crawfords’ hilltop home, surrounded by bushland in the Lockyer Valley.
Robert Crawford was described as a “love rat” who was motivated to kill his wife because he stood to lose financially in a divorce settlement brought on by his serial infidelity.
The former pilot faced the loss of his beloved $2m home and his early retirement plans if his wife followed through with divorce plans, jurors were told.
“He knew he stood to lose out,” crown prosecutor Chris Cook said.
“That’s why he was telling his lovers all about it.”
Referred to as a “master manipulator”, Robert Crawford embarked on a plan to make his wife’s death appear like a tragic accident, the jury was told.
“It was Mr Crawford who caused Mrs Crawford’s body to be at the bottom of the retaining wall of the property,” Cook said.

“It was Mr Crawford who also moved the lawnmower over the retaining wall.”
Robert Crawford’s defence had attacked the case against him as full of gaps filled in with speculation and wrongful suspicion.
“It is one of the weakest circumstantial cases you will ever see in a criminal court,” Robert Crawford’s barrister Saul Holt KC said.
The defence said he had engaged in multiple infidelities and lied about them but was trying to repair his marriage before his wife suffered an accident.
Robert Crawford had been busy with work calls and had let his wife move the lawnmower away from automated lawn sprinklers, Holt said.
But the prosecution said Frances Crawford would not have gone outside in her pyjamas in zero-degree weather to move an almost 250kg lawnmower that her children had never seen her use.
Robert Crawford, who was on bail throughout the trial, awaits sentencing.
